text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended lower across the board following the absence of any fresh constructive news. October gave up $1.30 to close at $328.50 while December lost $0.90 to close at $324.00 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended a dull session broadly lower. The most-active October contract closed down 4 points at 11.66 cents/lb, while second-position March settled 9 points lower at 11.86 cents/lb. There was no fresh news to influence prices.

EUROPE - Western Europe's sugar beet areas turned drier during the week ended July 29. Industry sources in Northern Germany said that sugar beet yields should be higher than last year due to favourable weather. In Spain crop conditions are stable, but soil moisture is declining in the north. In Eastern Europe, heavy rainfall eased in Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia. Beet crop potential is stable and the weather outlook for a slightly drier trend should keep prospects near average. In the sugar beet growing areas of the former Soviet Union, rains eased during the week ended July 29. Rains totalling 180 to 300 per cent of normal in the Ukraine could have a slightly negative impact, but drier weather expected in the first half of August, could improve crop potential. Elsewhere near normal rainfall in July in western Russia and in the western Volga valley could raise yields above average.

NORWAY ** - Sugar imports in June 1997 amounted to 17,117 tonnes, raw value, up from 15,822 tonnes in June 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first six months of 1997 (January/June) up to 88,530 tonnes, slightly up on the 86,564 tonnes imported in the corresponding period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 188,832 tonnes against 173,712 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in 1997 were Denmark with 40,654 tonnes whites against 52,916 tonnes, the UK with 24,038 tonnes compared to 20,122 tonnes and Sweden with 12,069 tonnes against 2,557 tonnes.

SOUTH KOREA ** - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 71,215 tonnes, up from 62,327 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1997 (January/February) up to 254,738 tonnes compared to 251,243 tonnes in 1996. Total imports in 1996 amounted to 1.399 million tonnes against 1.306 million tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in January/February 1997 were Australia with 174,748 tonnes raws against 166,214 tonnes, Thailand with 59,981 tonnes compared to 62,912 tonnes and South Africa with 19,979 tonnes, up from 2,000 tonnes.

Sugar exports in February 1997 reached 16,248 tonnes, down from 24,919 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative exports in January/February 1997 up to 52,456 tonnes compared to 69,461 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1996 amounted to 300,637 tonnes, up from 247,235 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of destination in 1997 were Hong Kong with 28,796 tonnes whites against 16,013 tonnes and Indonesia with 11,400 tonnes compared to 37,800 tonnes.
